headline: Bangladesh gets its first power from a nuclear plant

sources.title: Rooppur nuclear plant feeds 350MW into national grid for the first time (The Daily Star)

chunks.text: Bangladesh, a country of about 170 million people in South Asia, got electricity from nuclear power for the first time on November 17, 2026. Its first nuclear power plant was {{hooked up}} to the national [[grid]]. A grid is the [[network]] of [[power lines]] that carries electricity to homes and businesses. Within 30 minutes, the plant was {{putting out}} 350 megawatts. A megawatt is one million watts, a [[unit]] for measuring electric power.

verbs.correct: To connect something to a system
verbs.why: Workers hook up new homes to the city water system. The cable company hooks up our internet in one day. On November 17, 2026, Bangladesh's first nuclear power plant was hooked up to the national grid.
This small engine puts out a lot of power. Big wind turbines put out energy all day. Within 30 minutes, the plant was putting out 350 megawatts.

chunks.text: The plant, in the west of the country, was built with help from Russia. Work on it {{kicked off}} in 2017. Its first [[reactor]] began making heat in October 2026. A reactor is the part of a power plant where [[nuclear fuel]] makes heat for electricity. The project {{fell behind}}, and its [[deadline]] is now June 2028. A stronger U.S. dollar also {{drove up}} the cost in Bangladesh's own money. Reports say the [[total cost]] will be about 11.2 billion dollars.

verbs.why: The school year kicks off in late August. Our town's summer festival kicks off with a parade. Work on the plant kicked off in 2017.

verbs.wrong: To be given a new name
verbs.why: Construction work often falls behind in bad weather. A road project falls behind when parts arrive late. The project fell behind, and its deadline is now June 2028.

verbs.correct: To make a cost or price higher
verbs.wrong: To split a cost in two
verbs.why: Bad weather drives up the price of fruit. A big sports event drives up hotel prices. A stronger dollar drove up the cost of the plant in Bangladesh's own money.

chunks.text: The plant is now in a [[trial period]]. During the tests, engineers want to {{figure out}} how the plant and the grid work together. Under the test plan, the plant is [[disconnected]] at times for [[technical checks]]. The reactor may also {{shut down}} for short periods. The power it makes will {{ramp up}} [[step by step]], with [[pauses]]. Bangladesh's nuclear [[safety agency]] must {{sign off on}} each new step.

verbs.correct: To discover how or why something happens
verbs.wrong: To make something work much faster
verbs.why: Doctors run tests to figure out what is wrong. A mechanic figures out why a car makes a strange noise. Engineers want to figure out how the plant and the grid work together.

verbs.correct: To stop working for a while
verbs.wrong: To be moved to a new site
verbs.why: Our office computers shut down for updates at night. Some factories shut down for a week every summer. The reactor may also shut down for short periods during the trial.
Production ramps up slowly at a new factory. Ticket sales ramp up in the weeks before a big concert. The power the plant makes will ramp up step by step, with pauses.
The manager signs off on every new hire. A city inspector signs off on each new building. Bangladesh's nuclear safety agency must sign off on each new step.

chunks.text: The science minister said the tests may {{go on}} through December and January. He hoped the reactor would reach its [[full power]] of 1,200 megawatts by early February 2027. With a second reactor planned for 2028, the plant is expected to supply about 11 percent of the country's electricity. Bangladesh gets about half of its electricity from natural gas. It has faced power [[shortages]] for years. The plant should help it {{cut down on}} [[imported]] fuel.

verbs.why: The meeting often goes on until late at night. In the spring, the rain goes on for days. The minister said the tests may go on through December and January.
My doctor tells me to cut down on salt. Many families cut down on driving when gas is expensive. The plant is expected to help Bangladesh cut down on imported fuel.

mainIdea.s: Bangladesh sent power from its first nuclear plant into the national grid on November 17, 2026. Tests are still going on, and officials hope its first reactor will reach full power in early 2027.
mainIdea.why: The plant was hooked up to the grid for the first time. Tests will go on, and the science minister hopes for full power by early February 2027.

mainIdea.s: Bangladesh's new nuclear plant now gives steady power to homes across the country every day. Officials say all testing is finished and that a second reactor will start working next month.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the plant is only in a trial period. The reactor may shut down during tests, and the second reactor is planned for 2028.

mainIdea.s: Bangladesh has signed a deal with several countries to build large solar farms along its southern coast. These farms are meant to replace old gas plants by the end of the next ten years.
mainIdea.why: No solar deal is described. The country's first nuclear power plant was hooked up to the national grid on November 17, 2026.

tf.s: Bangladesh's first nuclear power plant was hooked up to the national grid.
tf.why: On November 17, 2026, the plant was hooked up to the grid and began sending electricity into it.

tf.s: The plant is already running at full power all the time.
tf.why: The plant is in a trial period. The tests may go on through December and January.

tf.s: Work on the nuclear power plant fell behind.
tf.why: The project fell behind, and its deadline is now June 2028.

tf.s: Bangladesh built the plant alone, with no help from another country.
tf.why: It was built with help from Russia. Work on the plant kicked off in 2017.

tf.s: A safety agency must sign off on each new step of the tests.
tf.why: Bangladesh's nuclear safety agency must sign off on each new step before the power ramps up.

tf.s: The plant is meant to make Bangladesh use more imported fuel.
tf.why: The plant is expected to help the country cut down on imported fuel.

lines.text: Did you hear that Bangladesh is getting electricity from nuclear power now?
Since November 17. Its first nuclear plant was {{hooked up}} to the national grid.
How much power is it {{putting out}}?
About 350 megawatts so far. But it's only a test, so the power is [[on and off]].
The reactor may {{shut down}} for short periods while engineers check things.
Who decides when it can do more?
A safety agency has to {{sign off on}} each new step. The tests may {{go on}} through January.
I read that the project {{fell behind}}.
It did. The deadline is now June 2028. [[These things take time]].
A stronger dollar {{drove up}} the price. Reports say it could reach about 11.2 billion dollars.
No, it isn't. But the plant should help the country {{cut down on}} imported fuel.
So people there must have [[high hopes]] for it.
They do. [[All in all]], it's a big day for the country.
